title: An Easy Way To Keep Your Cool When Students Misbehave nts-misbehave/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Revisiting reader-favorite advice, Linsin offers a simple mental model for staying calm while enforcing consequences: think like a referee. A referee, he explains, applies a fixed rule book automatically and without personal judgment, blowing the whistle the instant a foul occurs and issuing the specified consequence without hesitation, fear, or anger. He contrasts a consistent referee, under whom play is smooth and fair, with an inconsistent one who inserts personal feelings and loses control of the game. Applying the analogy directly to teaching, Linsin argues that teachers who base consequences on mood, favoritism, or perceived severity — rather than on a fixed classroom management plan — similarly lose control, breeding anger and resentment among students. The referee metaphor is offered as a practical, memorable tool teachers can use in the moment to detach personal emotion from the act of enforcing rules.
points: Thinking like a referee — applying rules automatically and without personal judgment — helps teachers stay calm when enforcing consequences.
A good referee follows a fixed rule book consistently, which keeps a game (or classroom) fair and under control.
Inconsistent enforcement based on mood or bias causes players — or students — to grow angry and resentful.
Consequences should be delivered with no hesitation, fear, or anger, immediately upon witnessing misbehavior.
Consistent, referee-like enforcement gives teachers both control of the classroom and personal peace of mind.
quotes: The advice is this: When enforcing consequences, think like a referee.
A referee’s job is to make sure players abide by the agreed-upon rules of the game. That’s it. They make no judgments or decisions of their own accord.
A good referee is defined by their calm and consistent adherence to the rule book—the purpose of which is to make the game safe and fair for all participants.
Teachers who are inconsistent and enforce consequences based on how the misbehavior makes them feel, who is doing the misbehaving, or the perceived severity of the misbehavior also lose control.
As soon as a student strays from your rule book ( classroom management plan ), follow through like a referee in the Super Bowl.
Because when you focus on being a good referee, not only will you have excellent control of your class, but keeping your cool will be easy.
